```{r}
#| include: false
# library(): loads a package so its functions can be used in this session.
# normalizePath(): resolves a path into a canonical absolute path.
# getwd(): returns the current working-directory path.
# file.exists(): checks whether each specified file path exists.
# file.path(): joins path components with the platform-appropriate separator.
# dirname(): returns the directory portion of a file path.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
library(knitr)
project <- normalizePath(getwd())
while (!file.exists(file.path(project, "20261.Rproj")) && dirname(project) != project) project <- dirname(project)
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(project, "20261.Rproj")))
```
## 1. Mechanisms

Binomial: fixed three customers, binary purchase outcome, common probability 0.30, independent decisions. Group shopping or changing purchase probabilities undermines this model. Poisson counts require a justified constant-rate process with independent increments and no batch arrivals; a changing arrival rate or clustered arrivals undermines that model. The count alone does not establish either model.

## 2. Binomial answers

```{r}
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# dbinom(): returns binomial point probabilities for size trials and success probability prob.
# pbinom(): returns P(X<=q) for binomial counts; lower.tail=FALSE gives P(X>q).
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# names(): reads or assigns names to vector elements or table columns.
# unname(): removes names or dimension names without changing the underlying values.
# sqrt(): returns the nonnegative square root of a nonnegative number.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# abs(): returns absolute values; a small tolerance in an equality check permits floating-point rounding.
a <- c(Exactly_two=dbinom(2,3,.3),At_most_two=pbinom(2,3,.3),
       At_least_two=pbinom(1,3,.3,lower.tail=FALSE),More_than_two=pbinom(2,3,.3,lower.tail=FALSE))
kable(data.frame(Event=names(a),Probability=unname(a)),digits=3)
kable(data.frame(Mean=3*.3,Variance=3*.3*.7,SD=sqrt(3*.3*.7)),digits=6)
stopifnot(abs(a[1]-.189)<1e-12,abs(a[3]-.216)<1e-12)
```

Answers: 0.189, 0.973, 0.216, 0.027. Mean 0.9, variance 0.63, SD 0.793725. `dbinom` returns a mass at one count; `pbinom` sums masses up to its boundary. At least two is more than one, so the upper-tail boundary is 1.

## 3. Poisson answers

```{r}
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# dpois(): returns Poisson count probabilities; lambda is the mean for the stated exposure.
# ppois(): returns P(X<=q) for Poisson counts; lower.tail=FALSE gives P(X>q).
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# names(): reads or assigns names to vector elements or table columns.
# unname(): removes names or dimension names without changing the underlying values.
lambda3 <- 10*3/15
a <- c(No_arrivals_3min=dpois(0,lambda3),At_least_two_3min=ppois(1,lambda3,lower.tail=FALSE),
       More_than_ten_15min=ppois(10,10,lower.tail=FALSE))
kable(data.frame(Event=names(a),Probability=unname(a)),digits=6)
```

Mean count in three minutes: 2. Probabilities: 0.135335, 0.593994, 0.416960. There is no fixed number of trials or finite upper count in the model. Mean 10 refers to 15 minutes and must be scaled to the requested exposure.

## 4. Simulation

```{r}
# set.seed(): fixes the pseudorandom sequence so rerunning the same code reproduces its artificial draws.
# rbinom(): generates artificial success counts; size is trials per count and prob is success probability.
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# pbinom(): returns P(X<=q) for binomial counts; lower.tail=FALSE gives P(X>q).
# mean(): computes an average; logical TRUE/FALSE values contribute 1/0, giving a proportion.
set.seed(307312)
y <- rbinom(10000,size=3,prob=.3)
kable(data.frame(Exact=pbinom(1,3,.3,lower.tail=FALSE),Simulated=mean(y>=2)),digits=6)
```

Accept a reproducible proportion near 0.216, with simulation variability acknowledged. Simulation evaluates implications of chosen assumptions; it provides no independent evidence of real store fit.

## 5. Without replacement

Successive selections from a finite set generally change the composition, creating dependent indicators and changing conditional success probabilities. A hypergeometric model may be appropriate for a fixed finite list with a fixed number of successes; that method is deferred, not silently replaced with a binomial calculation.
